rhythm.value: Detector: 23 shots, median 1.17 s. Corrected: 30 shots (7 splits, one cut moved 0.1 s earlier), median 0.95 s, 48 cuts per minute, with text swaps counted. Only two sequences hold longer than 2 s (4.03 s cards, 2.67 s interface); the end card is 2.86 s. Music-led, no voice. Sound was not heard: everything on sound is from audio.json and sync.json. Tempo is 130.06 BPM (confidence 0.71, beatRegularity 0.98), so the grid is believable. Cuts on beat 0.545 vs chance 0.346 overall, but with corrected times after 10.5 s only 9 of 21 land on a beat (local chance 0.35), which is no evidence. Against onsets 19 of 21 hit (local chance 0.70), so cuts follow transients, not the bar. Those onsets may be hits placed on the cuts rather than music the cuts follow: the data cannot separate the two. Before 10.5 s, in the quiet section, it reverses: 5 of 8 land on a beat (local chance 0.35) and 1 of 8 on an onset (chance 0.18), on too few cuts to prove it.

value.description: The graph is the transition. Five centred bars enter from the bottom at F103; by F105 they are at 30-55% height, then they slow to a near-plateau for 6 frames (F107-F111) so the shape reads as a chart; from F111 to F114 they surge to fill the frame edge to edge. Hairline gaps between bars remain visible for a frame, then the next line rises on the now solid blue from F115, starting low and decelerating over 8 frames.
value.why: A wipe that means something: money rises and becomes the next scene. The plateau is the key choice, since a linear fill would read only as a wipe.
value.name: element-grows-to-ground

value.description: Radial gauge race, then hold. Hard cut in on the first value. Roughly 90-100 radial ticks (not counted exactly) fill clockwise while the value races on every frame: 2, 7, 25, 41, 52, 61, 68, 74, 78, 82, 86, 88, 91, 93, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 99, 100 (thousands) over F396-F416, 61% of the way by the 5th frame (power3.out). The top value then holds 0.47 s while the whole gauge pulls back on an accelerating curve (diff 1.9 at F417 to 8.6 at F429), cut at F431 on an onset (0.017 s from one).
value.why: Expo-out counters feel like momentum that arrives rather than a meter being read. The 0.5 s hold is what lets $100K land before the cut takes it away.
value.name: front-loaded-number-race

value.description: The button eats the interface. A light band sweeps in from both edges of the button (F381-F389), the label shrinks away as the button grows (F388-F391), and by F395 it is about 94% of the frame width. It cuts on F396, before fully covering, to a contrasting white ground, not to the blue the viewer expects.
value.why: The action is enlarged until it is all there is, and the cut gives a hit of relief. Cutting before it fills avoids a dull beat of plain colour.
value.name: button-swells-cut-before-fill

value.description: You are first. A profit figure runs up on white (F491-F513). Hard cut to a ranking streaming vertically under motion blur, with one wider row pinned at centre carrying that same green figure and labelled '(You)'. Rows settle in 0.5 s and the stack slides up until the pinned row is on top (F515-F555). Then a hard punch-in on the top four rows at F557, with a slow sheen travelling along the first row.
value.why: Before it says what winning pays, it shows the viewer already winning, and the figure links the two shots so the row reads as the same person.
value.name: pinned-row-ranking-stream

value.description: Word and digit pair. The word enters low in frame at F581 and travels up and left as the number field opens beside it (F583); 10, 14, 19, 23, 27, 32, 36, 39, 43, 46, 48, 49, 50 by F595: near even steps that slow only in the last four frames (power1.out), not a strong expo-out. A hard cut to the sentence at 56% of that size follows, and the words of the second line arrive 1-3 frames apart.
value.why: The size drop from number to sentence tells the viewer the headline is over and its meaning follows, so no transition is needed.
value.name: word-counter-then-sentence-drop
